**About 300–400 W of solar recharges a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in one sunny day.** 200 W is a common budget pairing, but it takes about 1.5 days.

## The math

**Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7–0.75)**

The 0.7–0.75 factor accounts for heat, panel angle and charge-controller losses. Panels rarely deliver their rated watts outdoors ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).

| Panel size | Energy per day (4.5 peak sun hours) | Time to refill 1,000 Wh |
|---|---|---|
| 100 W | ~315 Wh | ~3 days |
| 200 W | ~630 Wh | ~1.5 days |
| 300 W | ~950 Wh | ~1 day |
| 400 W | ~1,260 Wh | under 1 day |

For a full refill in one day, you need about 270 W with 5 sun hours, about 340 W with 4, and about 450 W with 3 ([power-runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)). In a northern winter with about 2 sun hours, you'd need 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Rule of thumb:** divide battery Wh by 5. That gives about 200 W for a 1,000 Wh station, which refills it in about 1.5 days of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

## Check your station before buying
1. **Maximum solar input (W).** If your station caps solar input at 200 W, a 400 W panel won't charge it faster in full sun. A somewhat larger panel still helps on cloudy days and in morning or evening light.
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay within the station's range. Too much voltage can damage the station. Be especially careful if you wire panels in series.
3. **Connector.** Make sure you have the right adapter, such as MC4 to XT60 or DC barrel plugs.

## One option at 400 W
The **ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel** costs $299. Code ALLPOWERS26 reportedly takes it to about $269 (checked Oct 21, valid through Dec 30). Specs:
- Voc 45.3 V, so it works with stations that accept roughly 12–60 V solar input.
- Too high-voltage for some small stations, such as the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2.
- Heavy for a folding panel at 18.5 kg (about 41 lb).
